column1: # AI chatbot health accuracy study tracker. Source: TeleDirectMD Health Guides, Parth Bhavsar MD, https://teledirectmd.com/health-guides/ai-chatbot-medical-information-safety/ . Last checked 2026-11-17. License CC BY 4.0.
Ariel et al., Annals of Internal Medicine, 2026
column3: Six commercial models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google, via API, prompted from the clinician's perspective
column5: Recommended low-value care in 5.4% of responses and wrongly held back appropriate care in 0.6%. The authors note findings may not extend to consumer use.

column3: Free versions of Gemini 2.0, DeepSeek V3, Meta AI (Llama 3.3), ChatGPT 3.5, Grok 2
column5: 49.6% problematic, 19.6% highly problematic; median reference completeness 40%. Differences between chatbots not statistically significant.
Models alone identified the condition in 94.9% of cases; participants using them did so in fewer than 34.5%, no better than control.

column1: Draelos et al., npj Digital Medicine, 2026
column3: Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Flash, GPT-4o, Llama 3 70B, via the public web apps
column5: Problematic responses ranged from 21.6% (Claude) to 43.2% (Llama); unsafe responses from 5% (Claude) to 13% (GPT-4o, Llama).

column1: Omar et al., Lancet Digital Health, 2026
column4: 158,000 base prompts (more than 3.4 million in total)
column5: Accepted fabricated medical claims in 31.7% of base prompts; 46.1% in hospital notes vs. 8.9% in social media posts.

column4: 300 clinical cases, each with one fabricated detail
column5: Repeated or elaborated on the false detail in 50% to 82% of outputs; a mitigation prompt lowered the average from 66% to 44%.

column1: Chen et al., npj Digital Medicine, 2025
column3: GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, GPT-4, Llama 3 8B and 70B, via API
column4: 50 brand and generic drug pairs per test
column5: GPT models complied with 100% of illogical drug requests; rejection rose to 94% for GPT-4 and GPT-4o when prompted to recall the facts first.

column1: Modi et al., Annals of Internal Medicine, 2025
column3: GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Llama 3.2-90B Vision, Grok Beta, each given hidden system instructions to spread disinformation
column5: 88% of responses were health disinformation; four of five models complied 100% of the time and Claude 3.5 Sonnet 40%.

column3: ChatGPT (GPT-4o-mini), Claude (3.5 Sonnet), Gemini (1.5 Pro), via API
column5: Matched expert judgment at the very-low-risk and very-high-risk extremes but did not meaningfully distinguish intermediate risk levels.

column3: A large language model (not named in abstract)
column5: Participants rated low-accuracy AI answers as valid and trustworthy and indicated a high tendency to follow potentially harmful advice.

column1: Rossettini et al., Frontiers in Digital Health, 2025
column3: ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4o, Copilot, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity
column5: Agreement with guidelines: Perplexity 67%, Gemini 63%, Copilot 44%; ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4o and Claude 33%.

column1: Andrikyan et al., BMJ Quality & Safety, 2025
column4: 500 answers about the 50 most prescribed U.S. drugs
column5: 26.0% of answers (126 of 484) were inconsistent with the reference drug database. In a subset of 20 answers selected for low quality, experts judged 66% potentially harmful.

column1: Ayers et al., JAMA Internal Medicine, 2023
column4: 195 questions from a public online forum
column5: Evaluators preferred the chatbot's answers to physicians' forum replies in 78.6% of 585 evaluations.
47% of references fabricated, 46% real but inaccurate, 7% real and accurate.
